use_case.title: Governance in Testing
use_case.author: Steve Zeller
use_case.problem: Regulated companies have to prove that every software change was tested and approved before release. Most test automation doesn't produce that proof on its own: scripts can be changed by anyone, evidence is collected by hand, and AI-written tests can behave differently from run to run. The result is slow releases, audit findings, or both.
use_case.position: Leapwork helps regulated enterprises test with control: standards enforced through review and approval, every test change logged and versioned, and deterministic tests that run the same way every time.

industries.drives_need: SOX: auditors sample changes to financial systems and expect proof each was tested and approved before release.
GxP: systems used in regulated work must be validated, with documented test evidence and approvals.
Change control and resilience rules: DORA in the EU requires testing changes before release plus end-to-end and performance testing; PCI DSS requires approved, tested changes to card systems.
Patient safety: NHS organizations can't deploy health IT without clinical safety sign-off; EHR upgrades and migrations need full regression. US HIPAA is about data protection, a weaker driver.

personas.cares_about: One standard across teams; releases they can sign off.
Evidence that satisfies FDA and EU rules.
Proof every change was tested and approved.

pain_points.title: Proving every change was tested and approved.
pain_points.detail: Auditors sample changes and expect a test record and sign-off for each.
pain_points.fix: Versioned tests that move from draft to review to published; only authorized roles can publish.

pain_points.title: Gathering audit evidence by hand.
pain_points.detail: SAP teams spend weeks collecting screenshots for SOX.
pain_points.fix: Every run keeps the test version, logs and a video, exportable via API.

pain_points.title: Slow, manual validation.
pain_points.detail: GxP tests are run and documented by hand, and the tool itself must be validated.
pain_points.fix: No-code automation across SAP, Oracle, Dynamics, Salesforce and desktop apps; GxP-validated managed service via Pharma IT.

pain_points.title: Playwright tests with no controls.
pain_points.detail: Code-based suites lack approvals, roles and an audit trail.
pain_points.fix: Adds login, roles, scheduling, approvals and audit logs around Playwright.

pain_points.title: AI-written tests that vary run to run.
pain_points.detail: A growing concern for QA leaders adopting AI.
pain_points.fix: AI writes tests from requirements and links each to its source; tests run as fixed code with no AI at runtime.

pain_points.title: Performance testing outside the audit trail.
pain_points.detail: DORA requires performance testing, often run in a separate, ungoverned tool.
pain_points.fix: Performance, load and API testing with role-based access and exportable audit logs.

use_case.pain_points_note: Review, approval and role-based access in Flow are Enterprise Edition features.
